steps.title: Open the Research home
steps.narration: We open Trendora's Research home. Everything shown here is forward-tested evidence pooled from stored daily snapshots — descriptive history, never a predicted or fabricated number.
steps.point_out: The page opens on the existing Factor Lab and its decile sort; this iteration adds a brand-new Setup & Pattern Lab lower down the same page.

steps.title: Reveal the new Setup & Pattern Lab event study
steps.narration: Scrolling down reveals this iteration's new Setup & Pattern Lab. Pick any setup or detected chart pattern and it pools every past occurrence across all snapshots, then reports — for each forward horizon — the return distribution, expectancy, best/worst excursion (MAE/MFE) and downside-only risk-adjusted ratios.
steps.point_out: The Subject dropdown (grouped Setups vs Patterns) and the per-horizon distribution & exit-horizon table. It opens on 'Actionable', a genuinely rare setup with only about two occurrences — so every value honestly reads NA with its n=2 warning instead of inventing a number. Choosing a data-rich subject such as Breakout-watch fills the very same table with real percentages and a highlighted best exit-horizon.

steps.title: Follow the page's shared Horizon control to 60 days
steps.narration: The lab has no date picker of its own. It follows the page's single shared Horizon control — switching it to 60 days re-points every panel to the 60-day forward window.
steps.point_out: One control drives the whole page; there is deliberately no second date selector to fall out of sync.

steps.title: Read the event study at the 60-day horizon
steps.narration: Back in the lab, the entire study has re-pointed to 60 days, and below the distribution table it breaks the chosen subject down by market regime and by sector for that horizon.
steps.point_out: The meta now reads 'Pooled occurrences (60d)', and the 'By market regime (60d)' and 'By sector (60d)' panels follow. Every configured regime still gets its own row — empty or thin ones shown honestly as NA + n=0, never a fabricated zero — and only sectors that actually have members appear.
